description.ncbi_summary: Prostaglandin-D synthase is a sigma class glutathione-S-transferase family member. The enzyme catalyzes the conversion of PGH2 to PGD2 and plays a role in the production of prostanoids in the immune system and mast cells. The presence of this enzyme can be used to identify the differentiation stage of human megakaryocytes. [provided by RefSeq, Jul 2008].

uniprot_function.text: Bifunctional enzyme which catalyzes both the conversion of PGH2 to PGD2, a prostaglandin involved in smooth muscle contraction/relaxation and a potent inhibitor of platelet aggregation, and the conjugation of glutathione with a wide range of aryl halides and organic isothiocyanates (PubMed:10824118, PubMed:11672424, PubMed:12244105, PubMed:12627223, PubMed:15113825, PubMed:16547010, PubMed:17519235, PubMed:19939518, PubMed:9353279, PubMed:9425264). Similarly, catalyzes the conversion of PGH3 (derived from eicosapentaenoate (EPA, C20:5n-3)) to PGD3, though PGH2 remains the preferred substrate (PubMed:17519235). Also exhibits low glutathione-peroxidase activity towards cumene hydroperoxide.
